purpose: Target-neutral semantics of a dense-memory wrapper leaf. Behavioral, G0 register and G1 macro providers must all meet this contract; the geometry ADR enumerates the shapes a target accepts.
semantics_rule: The semantics values are binding and validated by model/dense_memory.py; the prose fields below explain them. A different value is a different contract and must change the model and its tests.

legal_shapes.rule: A masked shape has one write-mask bit per 8-bit byte. An unmasked shape, such as a tag array, has one mask bit for the whole word.

throughput: One read or one write per cycle. A dual-port or read-during-write form is a separate contract, not a parameter of this one.
polarity: Enable, write enable and write-mask bits are active high at the wrapper. Providers convert to macro polarity.
output_hold: Read data is defined only in the cycle read_latency cycles after the read was accepted. In every other cycle, including after a write, an idle cycle or reset, the output is unknown; consumers register what they need.
enable_low: When enable is low, write enable, address, data and mask are ignored and may be unknown.
write_mask: A write changes exactly the bytes whose mask bit is set. A write with an all-zero mask is a legal no-op that still uses the port.
collision: The single port cannot read and write in one cycle. A read accepted in the cycle after a write to the same address returns the written bytes.
reset: Payload is not reset. Reset drops in-flight reads and makes the output unknown; array contents are unchanged.
unknown_data: Unwritten bytes and bytes written with unknown data read as unknown. An enabled request with an unknown or out-of-range address, an unknown write enable, or a wrong-width mask is illegal.
